title: Reuse and cleanup
current: Lane lookup uses the public item reference and recorded branches; cleanup acts on a recorded branch, or on detached@<commit> when the checkout has no branch. A done item's lanes retire on the machine that holds them once each proves clean and landed; a preserved lane is named with its reason. One malformed lane in a prune batch is reported and skipped; the other lanes in that batch are still judged. A clean detached lane whose commit is on the target retires; a dirty or unmerged detached lane stays, with the reason named. A cancelled item's lanes are deleted outright — worktree (even dirty, locked or unmerged), local branch and origin branch — by the cancel on its own machine and by the next merged-lane sweep on every other machine, and each deletion's head SHAs land in the item's Progress Log under `Cancelled lanes deleted`. A standalone landing retires the item's own lanes and then runs the machine-wide merged-lane sweep. A deployment run's member close-out retires only that member's lanes; after every member has closed, the run runs that sweep once per distinct checkout. Run close-out prints each preserved lane as a `Lane cleanup warning:` with the doctor repair. A hosted control plane settles runs where no lane lives, so lane creation at the `max_active_worktrees` cap runs the same sweep first and then refuses only for what remains, naming unmerged lanes to merge, landed lanes and finished deploy-run driver trees for `yoke watch doctor -- --only HC-worktree-health --fix`, and an open run's driver tree as in use.
